claims.text: The July 29, 2025 joint Scattered Spider advisory describes attackers gathering password-reset information through calls, then persuading IT help-desk personnel to reset passwords and/or transfer MFA tokens, enabling account takeovers in SSO environments.
The same advisory recommends phishing-resistant MFA, including FIDO/WebAuthn or PKI-based implementations. The recovery-reset tactic is not evidence that all MFA is useless.

The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security urges organizations covered by the Scattered Spider advisory to regularly test their cyber security business processes, including those used by their service providers.
A review limited to the normal sign-in screen can miss how identity is re-established during account recovery.
Ask who can authorize a recovery reset, what independent evidence they require, and what happens when the normal proof is unavailable.

counterevidence: The same advisory recommends phishing-resistant MFA. Do not write MFA is pointless, all recovery processes fail, or a checklist guarantees safety.
